paragraphs.title: The Covenant and the Rebels' Preparations

easy.explanation: The verse says, “In the seventh year Jehoiada strengthened himself.”
easy.q: Who strengthened himself in the seventh year?

easy.explanation: Jehoiada took the captains of hundreds into covenant with him.
easy.q: Whom did Jehoiada take into covenant with him?

easy.explanation: They gathered from Judah and came to Jerusalem.
easy.q: Where did the Levites and the chief of the fathers come?

answers: To establish the king’s son as ruler
medium.explanation: The covenant supported the reign of the king’s son according to the LORD’s word.
medium.q: What was the purpose of the covenant made in the house of God?

answers: To organize support for restoring the Davidic monarchy
To establish the house of Baal
medium.explanation: He gathered them to make a covenant and support the rightful king.
medium.q: Why did Jehoiada gather the commanders, Levites, and family leaders?

answers: He became determined and took action
medium.explanation: The phrase describes Jehoiada becoming prepared and resolved to act.
medium.q: In this context, what does “strengthened himself” mean?

answers: The covenant was meant to abolish the monarchy
The covenant prepared leaders and people to support his reign
The covenant concerned only Levitical service
challenge.explanation: The covenant led to the declaration that the king’s son should reign.
challenge.q: What connection between the covenant and the king’s son appears in these verses?

answers: The Levites did not come to Jerusalem
challenge.explanation: Gathering them from all Judah shows a wide organization of support.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from gathering the Levites out of all the cities of Judah?

answers: It shows that no king was needed
It presents the king’s reign as fulfilling the LORD’s word
It describes the building of Baal’s house
challenge.explanation: The people said the king’s son should reign as the LORD had spoken of David’s sons.
challenge.q: Why is the house of David mentioned?

paragraphs.title: Deploying the Guards and Protecting the King

easy.explanation: The instructions assigned duties to priests, Levites, and the people.
easy.q: Who were assigned to the guard positions?

easy.explanation: One third was stationed at the king’s house.
easy.q: Where was one third of the people stationed?

easy.explanation: He gave them spears, bucklers, and shields from the house of God.
easy.q: What weapons did Jehoiada give to the captains of hundreds?

answers: At the entrance, in the wilderness, and at Baal’s house
At the priests’ and Levites’ place, the king’s house, and the gate of the foundation
medium.explanation: The verses name these three locations for the divisions.
medium.q: How were the three groups divided?

answers: So there would be no interruption in the watch
To clear the house of the LORD
medium.explanation: Jehoiada dismissed not the courses, so both groups served together.
medium.q: Why were both those coming on the sabbath and those going out kept on duty?

answers: Keepers of the doors and gates
medium.explanation: Porters were guards assigned to the doors.
medium.q: What were the “porters of the doors”?

answers: To protect him on every side
To remove him from the house of God
To keep him away from the people
challenge.explanation: The Levites surrounded the king with their weapons in their hands.
challenge.q: What was the purpose of the Levites surrounding the king?

answers: They controlled access to the house
They were assigned only to sing
challenge.explanation: The command shows that unauthorized entry was forbidden.
challenge.q: What does the command that anyone entering the house should be put to death show about the guards?

answers: To defend the king and maintain the planned order
To give them to the priests of Baal
challenge.explanation: The weapons armed those protecting the king and the Temple.
challenge.q: Why were David’s weapons brought from the house of God?

paragraphs.title: Joash Is Crowned and Athaliah Is Removed

answers: He was crowned and anointed king
He was made a priest of Baal
easy.explanation: They put the crown upon him, made him king, and anointed him.

answers: The people running and praising the king
The priests worshipping in Baal’s house
easy.explanation: Athaliah heard the noise of the people running and praising the king.

answers: In the house of the LORD
At the entering of the horse gate by the king’s house
easy.explanation: She was killed at the entering of the horse gate by the king’s house.

answers: She rent her clothes and cried, “Treason, Treason”
medium.explanation: She rent her clothes and called the event treason.
medium.q: What did Athaliah do when she saw the king and the celebration?

answers: She was not to be slain in the house of the LORD
He wanted to make her queen
She was one of the Levites
medium.explanation: The priest specifically said, “Slay her not in the house of the LORD.”
medium.q: Why did Jehoiada order Athaliah to be taken out of the house of the LORD?

answers: A royal ornament placed on a ruler’s head
medium.explanation: The crown was placed upon Joash when he was made king.

answers: Joash is crowned, Athaliah discovers it, and she is removed
Baal’s house is destroyed, Athaliah is crowned, and the people rejoice
Athaliah dies, the Levites gather, and Joash is crowned
challenge.explanation: Joash is crowned first, Athaliah reacts, and she is then taken away and killed.
challenge.q: Which sequence of events is described?

answers: His royal position and connection to the law
challenge.explanation: They were presented as part of establishing Joash as king.
challenge.q: What do the crown and the testimony given to Joash represent?

answers: The people had already accepted and celebrated the new king
challenge.explanation: The people rejoiced and praised Joash rather than supporting her accusation.
challenge.q: Why was Athaliah’s cry of “Treason” not accepted by the people?

paragraphs.title: Renewing the Covenant with the LORD and Destroying Baal’s House

answers: Between himself, all the people, and the king
Between the Levites and the captains only
Between Athaliah and the priests of Baal
easy.explanation: Jehoiada made the covenant between himself, the people, and the king.
easy.q: Between whom did Jehoiada make a covenant?

easy.explanation: They agreed that they should be the LORD’s people.
easy.q: Whose people did they agree to be?

answers: They broke it down with its altars and images
easy.explanation: The people broke down the house of Baal and destroyed its altars and images.
easy.q: What did the people do to the house of Baal?

answers: The covenant renewed loyalty to the LORD, and destroying Baal’s house expressed that loyalty
medium.explanation: Their covenant commitment to the LORD was followed by removing Baal worship.
medium.q: What is the relationship between the covenant and the destruction of Baal’s house?

answers: They placed them at the gates
medium.explanation: The verse says they broke Baal’s images in pieces.
medium.q: What did the people do to Baal’s images?

medium.explanation: The expression means that the people demolished the house of Baal.

answers: A change from loyalty to Baal to loyalty to the LORD
A change from worshipping the LORD to worshipping Baal
challenge.explanation: The covenant affirmed the LORD, while Baal’s house and images were destroyed.
challenge.q: What religious change is shown by these two actions?

answers: It shows that Baal’s leadership was removed along with its shrine and images
It shows that Mattan was made king
It explains the appointment of the Levites
challenge.explanation: The verse records the removal of both the pagan priest and the place of worship.
challenge.q: Why is the killing of Mattan, Baal’s priest, also mentioned?

answers: The action was public and communal, not merely Jehoiada’s private decision
The destruction had no connection with the king
challenge.explanation: The verse emphasizes that all the people went to the house of Baal and destroyed it.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the fact that all the people broke down Baal’s house?

paragraphs.title: Restoring the Temple and the Kingdom

easy.explanation: Jehoiada appointed the offices of the house of the LORD through the priests and Levites.
easy.q: Who received responsibility for the service of the house of the LORD?

easy.explanation: The priests and Levites were appointed to offer the LORD’s burnt offerings.
easy.q: What offerings were made in the house of the LORD?

answers: It was emptied of its people
easy.explanation: The final verse says, “the city was quiet.”
easy.q: What was the condition of the city at the end of the chapter?

answers: Offerings, singing, and guarding the holiness of the Temple
Building Baal’s house and breaking the LORD’s altars
medium.explanation: The verses mention burnt offerings, singing, and guards preventing the unclean from entering.
medium.q: Which parts of Temple worship were restored?

answers: So that nothing unclean would enter
To admit the priests of Baal
medium.explanation: The porters guarded the entrances so the unclean could not enter.
medium.q: Why were the porters set at the gates of the house of the LORD?

answers: The people rejoiced and the city was quiet
The people fled and the city was destroyed
medium.explanation: The people rejoiced, and the city became quiet after Athaliah’s death.
medium.q: What happened after the king was set upon the throne?

answers: Both restored worship and royal authority brought order after Athaliah’s removal
challenge.explanation: The chapter ends with renewed worship, the king established, and peace in the city.
challenge.q: How did restoring Temple service help stabilize the kingdom?

answers: It followed the instructions of the law
It followed the laws of Baal
There were no instructions for the service
challenge.explanation: The phrase states that the offerings were made according to Moses’ law.
challenge.q: What does “as it is written in the law of Moses” show about the priests’ service?

answers: Worship is restored, the king is seated, the people rejoice, and the city is quiet
Baal’s house is destroyed, the people flee, and the king is removed
Athaliah is crowned, the Temple is rebuilt, and the Levites rejoice
challenge.explanation: The closing verses connect restored worship and royal order with public joy and peace.
challenge.q: What sequence of cause and effect appears at the end of the chapter?
